input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement is governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction.
input.rationale: Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which is outside the accepted list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales) and is close to the walk-away position of a foreign venue. It also directly conflicts with Section 28.2, which grants exclusive jurisdiction to the state and federal courts in New York County. We replaced only the jurisdiction words in 28.1 with New York law and deleted the redundant Singapore venue grant, so that Section 28.2's New York County forum controls; the Section 28.3 executive escalation process is acceptable and no arbitration clause exists in the document.

ops.oldText: governed exclusively by Singapore law, and the courts of Singapore have exclusive jurisdiction
ops.newText: governed exclusively by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws principles

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We changed the governing law in Section 28.1 from Singapore to New York, which is our standard position, and removed the conflicting grant of exclusive jurisdiction to the Singapore courts so that the exclusive venue provision in Section 28.2 (New York County) governs. If New York is not workable, we can accept Delaware or California law and courts, or England and Wales with the courts of London.
proposal.summary: Replace Singapore governing law and venue with New York law, leaving New York County courts as the exclusive forum.
